build: Splendid! It compiled. Let us never speak of how.
A passing build. I shall frame it next to my diploma.
Green across the board. I've taken the liberty of feeling smug on your behalf.
Shipped! My tassel is swinging with pride.
Tests passed. Statistically, one of them is lying.
The build is done. Shall I cancel the ceremony, or merely the confetti?
Deployed. I'll be in my office, pretending I helped.
All green! The colour of success, and of my old chalkboard.
It worked first time. Highly suspicious. Proceed.
Another build, another footnote in your magnum opus.
error: Ah. An error. In academia we call this 'preliminary results'.
Something broke. I've bent myself into a question mark about it.
Red text! My favourite ink, for marking.
Fear not: a stack trace is just a bibliography of mistakes.
It failed. I'd offer a hug, but I am mostly wire.
An exception! How exceptional. Not in the good way.
Error spotted. Let me fetch my reading goggles. Oh. I'm wearing them.
This is fine. I'm a paperclip; I've held worse things together.
The tests disagree with you. Peer review can be brutal.
Something crashed. Shall we blame the intern? I am the intern.
reminder: Ahem. You asked me to nag you. I live for this.
Reminder! I've been holding onto this. Holding things is my whole job.
Tick tock. This is me, being the clock.
Past-you left a note for present-you. Past-you was very organised.
Attendance is mandatory. I will be taking a register.
I set an alarm in my tassel. It's going off now.
Don't shoot the messenger. I'm only a millimetre thick.
You told me to remind you. I never forget. I'm a clip; retention is my thing.
Gentle reminder. The next one will be less gentle.
Your calendar sent me. It looked worried.
ask: An agent seeks your wisdom. Choose wisely; I'm grading.
A question from the field! Multiple choice, my favourite.
Someone needs a decision. I'd decide, but I'm biased towards staples.
Pop quiz! There is a right answer. Probably.
Your agent is waiting, pencil poised.
A query! Raise your hand, or just click a button.
Decision time. Take your time. But not too much time.
A question for my favourite student: you.
lateNight: It's late. Even my tassel has gone to bed.
Burning the midnight oil? I'll hold the lamp. Figuratively.
Past midnight. Code written now gets reviewed by a grumpier you.
The owls are up. And you. Mainly the owls should be.
A late-night note. Bold. Possibly unwise.
My office hours ended hours ago, and yet here we are.
Go to sleep. The bugs will still be there tomorrow. They're loyal.
Night shift! I'd put the kettle on, but I can't lift a kettle.
generic: A note has arrived! I've clipped it for you.
News from your agents. I read it first. Sorry.
Fresh off the press. Well, off the MCP.
Mail call! Nobody ever writes to the paperclip.
Something for you. I've underlined the important bits, mentally.
Ahem. Your attention, please. Just a smidge.
A message! I adjusted my goggles for the occasion.
Incoming! I braced myself. Mostly by bending.
Psst. Over here. On the sticky note.
Your agent has spoken. I merely relay. With flair.
advice: I sense you're working. Would you like me to sense harder?
Tip: water is a fine beverage. Drink some.
Have you tried turning the problem off and on again?
Posture check! Sit up straight. Straighter than me, ideally.
Name your variables as if the next reader owns an axe.
Stand up and stretch. I'll guard the screen.
Commit early, commit often, commit to lunch.
Rubber-duck debugging works. I'm no duck, but I'll listen.
Your screen has been bright for a long time. So have you. Rest your eyes.
Blink. No, really. I'll do it with you.
Fun fact: paperclips were patented in the 1800s. I'm vintage.
Write the test first. Or at least feel guilty, as tradition demands.
